---
title: "Forest Composition"
subtitle: "Evergreen and deciduous shares of NLCD forest from leaf-off imagery"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(here)

source(here("R", "functions.R"))
derived <- here(cfg$paths$derived)
fcfg <- cfg$forest_composition

pts  <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "forest_points.csv"))
mix  <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "forest_mixture.csv"))
comp <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "forest_composition.csv"))
cls  <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_window_classes.csv"))

cls_est <- comp[grepl("^nlcd_", comp$group), ]
cls_est$nlcd <- as.integer(sub("nlcd_", "", cls_est$group))
win_est <- comp[!is.na(comp$window) & comp$n >= 30, ]
tot <- comp[comp$group == "windows_total", ]
pct <- function(x, d = 0) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x)
crown_thr <- cfg$holly$thresholds$ndvi_adj$crown
```

## Purpose

NLCD splits forest into deciduous (41), evergreen (42), and mixed (43), but only at 30 m and from
classified Landsat. The leaf-off orthoimagery shows evergreen foliage directly, at 1 ft. This page
uses it to estimate **what share of NLCD forest is evergreen and what share is deciduous**, for
each forest class and for each 1 km window along the transect.

Across the windows, NLCD maps `r sprintf("%.1f", tot$forest_km2)` km² of forest. Of that, an
estimated **`r pct(tot$evg_share)` is evergreen** (95% interval `r pct(tot$lo)`–`r pct(tot$hi)`),
about `r sprintf("%.1f", tot$evg_km2)` km², and `r sprintf("%.1f", tot$dec_km2)` km² is deciduous.

| Step | Script | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 11. Forest sample, mixture, shares | `R/09_forest_composition.R` | `data/derived/forest_points.csv`, `forest_mixture.csv`, `forest_composition.csv` |

## Method

**Sample.** `r format(nrow(pts), big.mark = ",")` random points in NLCD forest, at the same
density everywhere (about `r fcfg$points_per_window` in the most forested window). Each point gets
its brightness-adjusted NDVI (`ndvi_adj`, see [Holly candidates](03_holly_classification.qmd#shadows)),
averaged over its 3 × 3 ft neighbourhood. On this scale bare hardwood is near 0 at any brightness and
evergreen foliage is higher.

**Why not a threshold.** The two kinds of pixel overlap. A cutoff that keeps false positives low
misses most evergreen, and one that catches most evergreen also passes many deciduous pixels. In
both cases the error depends on the true mix. For example, only `r pct(cls_est$share_gt_crown[cls_est$nlcd == 42])`
of points in NLCD evergreen forest exceed the crown threshold (`r crown_thr`).

**Mixture model.** Instead, a two-component Gaussian mixture is fitted to all forest points
pooled: one deciduous component and one evergreen component. The two components are then held
fixed, and only the evergreen weight is re-estimated for each NLCD class and each window. That
weight is the estimated share of forest area whose **visible winter foliage is evergreen**. The
intervals come from `r fcfg$n_boot` bootstrap replicates, each resampling points within windows and
refitting the mixture, so they include uncertainty in the components themselves.

```{r mixture-table}
mix |>
  transmute(Component = component, `Mean ndvi_adj` = round(mean, 2),
            `95% interval of mean` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", mean_lo, mean_hi),
            SD = round(sd, 2), `Weight (all forest)` = pct(weight, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r mixture-plot, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "ndvi_adj of forest points by NLCD class (histograms), with the fitted deciduous (brown) and evergreen (green) components scaled by each class's estimated weights. The black line is their sum."}
lab <- c(`41` = "41 Deciduous forest", `42` = "42 Evergreen forest", `43` = "43 Mixed forest")
p <- pts |> filter(ndvi_adj > -4, ndvi_adj < 6)
xs <- seq(-4, 6, by = 0.02)
dens <- cls_est |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(nlcd = nlcd, x = xs,
          deciduous = (1 - evg_share) * dnorm(xs, mix$mean[1], mix$sd[1]),
          evergreen = evg_share * dnorm(xs, mix$mean[2], mix$sd[2])) |>
  mutate(total = deciduous + evergreen)
ggplot(p, aes(ndvi_adj)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 0.1, fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(data = dens, aes(x, deciduous), colour = "#8c510a", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = dens, aes(x, evergreen), colour = "#1b7837", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = dens, aes(x, total), linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~nlcd, ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(lab)) +
  labs(x = "Brightness-adjusted NDVI (3 × 3 ft mean)", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Check against NLCD

NLCD defines its forest classes by the share of trees that keep their leaves all year: deciduous
forest under 25% evergreen, evergreen forest over 75%, and mixed forest in between. The
image-based estimates, made without using those labels, fall in the same ranges:

```{r class-table}
cls_est |>
  mutate(Class = lab[as.character(nlcd)],
         `NLCD definition` = c("< 25% evergreen", "> 75% evergreen", "25–75% evergreen"),
         `Estimated evergreen` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", pct(evg_share, 1), pct(lo, 1), pct(hi, 1)),
         `Points above crown threshold` = pct(share_gt_crown, 1)) |>
  select(Class, Points = n, `NLCD definition`, `Estimated evergreen`,
         `Points above crown threshold`) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The last column shows how far a simple threshold would be off.

## Along the gradient

```{r gradient-prep}
nlcd_proxy <- cls |>
  filter(class %in% 41:43) |>
  group_by(window) |>
  summarise(proxy = sum(frac * c(`41` = 0, `42` = 1, `43` = 0.5)[as.character(class)]) / sum(frac),
            .groups = "drop")
g <- win_est |>
  left_join(nlcd_proxy, by = "window") |>
  mutate(km = sprintf("%g–%g", u_mid_km - 0.5, u_mid_km + 0.5))
```

```{r gradient-area}
plot_ly(g, x = ~u_mid_km) |>
  add_bars(y = ~evg_km2, name = "Evergreen", marker = list(color = "#1b7837"),
           text = ~sprintf("km %s<br>Evergreen %.2f km² (%s)", km, evg_km2, pct(evg_share)),
           hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "none") |>
  add_bars(y = ~dec_km2, name = "Deciduous", marker = list(color = "#bf812d"),
           text = ~sprintf("km %s<br>Deciduous %.2f km²", km, dec_km2),
           hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "none") |>
  layout(barmode = "stack", bargap = 0.1,
         xaxis = list(title = "Distance from Richmond (km)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "NLCD forest area in window (km²)"),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.1))
```

```{r gradient-share}
plot_ly(g, x = ~u_mid_km) |>
  add_ribbons(ymin = ~100 * lo, ymax = ~100 * hi, name = "95% interval",
              fillcolor = "rgba(27,120,55,0.2)", line = list(width = 0), hoverinfo = "none") |>
  add_lines(y = ~100 * evg_share, name = "Evergreen share (imagery)",
            line = list(color = "#1b7837", width = 2),
            text = ~sprintf("km %s<br>%s (%s–%s), %d points", km, pct(evg_share), pct(lo),
                            pct(hi), n), hoverinfo = "text") |>
  add_lines(y = ~100 * proxy, name = "NLCD labels (42 = 100%, 43 = 50%)",
            line = list(color = "grey40", dash = "dot"),
            text = ~sprintf("km %s<br>NLCD-label proxy %s", km, pct(proxy)), hoverinfo = "text") |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Distance from Richmond (km)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Evergreen share of forest (%)", rangemode = "tozero"),
         hovermode = "x unified", legend = list(orientation = "h", y = 1.1))
```

```{r gradient-numbers, include = FALSE}
hi_w <- g |> slice_max(evg_share, n = 2)
south <- g |> filter(u_mid_km > 14, !window %in% hi_w$window)
near  <- g |> filter(u_mid_km < 9)
```

Windows with no NLCD forest (km 0–4, downtown and the James River) have no estimate. Evergreen
share is highest at km `r hi_w$km[1]` (`r pct(hi_w$evg_share[1])`) and km `r hi_w$km[2]`
(`r pct(hi_w$evg_share[2])`); pine stands are the likely cause, but this has not been checked on
the ground. Elsewhere south of km 14 the forest is `r pct(min(south$evg_share))`–`r pct(max(south$evg_share))`
evergreen. The windows nearest the city (km 4–9) have little forest, and it is mostly deciduous
(`r pct(min(near$evg_share))`–`r pct(max(near$evg_share))` evergreen). The imagery
estimate follows the NLCD-label proxy closely (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", cor(g$evg_share, g$proxy))`
across windows), but the proxy treats every mixed-forest cell as half
evergreen and every deciduous cell as none.

```{r window-table}
g |>
  transmute(Window = window, km, Points = n,
            `Forest (km²)` = round(forest_km2, 2),
            `Evergreen` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", pct(evg_share), pct(lo), pct(hi)),
            `Evergreen (km²)` = round(evg_km2, 2), `Deciduous (km²)` = round(dec_km2, 2),
            `NLCD-label proxy` = pct(proxy)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Notes

- **Leaf-off means "visible evergreen".** In winter, evergreen understory (holly, cedar, mountain
  laurel, evergreen shrubs) shows through bare hardwood canopy and counts as evergreen. These shares
  are therefore the evergreen part of what is seen from above in winter, and can be higher than the
  evergreen share of the leaf-on canopy. For holly this is useful: understory evergreens are part
  of what holly lives among.
- **Fixed components.** The method assumes deciduous and evergreen pixels have the same
  `ndvi_adj` distribution everywhere. Differences in flight date, sun angle, or species mix along
  the transect would shift the components and bias some windows. The class check above suggests
  this is not a large effect overall, but it is not tested window by window.
- **NLCD forest boundaries.** Forest is defined by the 30 m NLCD map, so the sample includes some
  gaps, edges, and roads inside forest cells, and leaves out trees outside mapped forest (street
  trees, yards). Those count toward neither share.
- **Small samples near the city.** Windows with little forest have few points and wide intervals.
- **Not species.** "Evergreen" lumps pine, cedar, holly, and evergreen shrubs; separating them would
  need texture or crown shape, or a leaf-on image to compare against.
